QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_40

question.text: A fund's return distribution shows kurtosis of 5.03. This is BEST described as:

answer.text: Leptokurtic — fatter tails and higher peak than normal, indicating elevated outlier risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.6.2: Kurtosis > 3 (excess kurtosis > 0) is LEPTOKURTIC — fatter tails, higher peak, more extreme outliers. 5.03 indicates elevated tail risk. The Trap: Option C describes platykurtic (<3). Option B describes normal (exactly 3). Option D is nonsensical. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B and XV test kurtosis interpretation. Manager's Pro-Tip: Kurtosis warnings are especially relevant for Cat III long-short or derivative-heavy funds. Supplement with a VaR analysis and a CVaR (expected shortfall) metric in the risk dashboard — one number is never sufficient.
